reasoning:
None of my hypotheses hold up consistently across rounds—not x-order, not color priority, not y-position—since each round contradicts the pattern from the previous one. I need to keep testing rather than commit to a rule yet.

Colour-first evidence is weak too, so it's not a reliable tiebreaker either. The order genuinely looks unpredictable from the scene. I'll stop flipping and simplify: drop the colour claim entirely from the annotator prompt since it's now contradicted, and keep increasing-x as the sole default since it has the most supporting evidence, while flagging it explicitly as a guess rather than a confirmed rule. I'll also update the subgoal clause that still references colour ordering to match.

At the button-press step, picking the "wrong" cube first still presumably works mechanically, even though the recorded trajectory marks it incorrect — I'll accept that residual discrepancy and move on to writing the edits.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: point at the first entry of the pending_cubes list as written at this step under the memory instruction (the highlighted cube with the smallest x, the robot's right-most, colour ignored), using that cube's current position,

edits.modify_from: and order the entries by colour first: blue cubes first, then red, then green, then any other colour; among cubes of the same colour, order by increasing x (the robot's right-most cube first, the left-most last). edits.modify_to: and order the entries by increasing x (the robot's right-most cube first, the left-most last). Colour plays no part and the order the areas are printed in plays no part. e.g. cubes at [57, 141], [70, 166], [92, 85] -> [[92, 85], [57, 141], [70, 166]].

edits.modify_from: The order is read from the episode, not computed from the scene: no coordinate sort reproduces it in every episode. In the episodes seen so far a blue highlighted cube is picked before a highlighted cube of any other colour; among cubes of the same colour the order varies.
edits.modify_to: The order is read from the episode, not computed from the scene: no coordinate sort and no colour priority reproduces it in every episode (increasing x, decreasing x, increasing y, decreasing y, printed-area order and blue-first have each been contradicted by at least one episode). The policy writes its list at the button-press step by increasing x as a fixed default; where the episode's pick order differs, annotate the true pick order anyway.

revision.refused: The report's decreasing-x ordering stays out. Across four rounds every candidate key has been contradicted: y both ways, printed order, reverse order, gripper and button distance (round 1), increasing x (rounds 3 and 4), blue-first (round 4), and now decreasing x (round 2). The pick order at the button-press step is therefore not predictable from the scene, and the annotator prompt now says so outright instead of carrying a remark that each round falsifies. What is committed is the removal of the colour priority, which this round contradicts and which only two single-episode observations ever supported, leaving increasing x as the fixed default guess, since it has the most episodes behind it and was the tie-break already in place; keeping one default stops the ordering from being rewritten every round. The annotated list keeps the true pick order, as in every round since round 1, so every step after the button press stays sufficient; the button-press step remains the one accepted residual guess. The sentence forbidding redirection to a cube of a different colour is kept: it is about matching the stored entry to the cube that was highlighted, not about ordering.
